items.title: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything): a new tool for decompiling and rebuilding app features
points: REA is an MCP server (a protocol/standard that lets AI agents access external tools) that decompiles apps by converting compiled code back into human-readable pseudocode
It works iteratively: you ask your agent to analyze a feature, REA returns pseudocode with evidence, and your agent refines until the feature is fully rebuilt without copying original code

Setup requires running 'npx rea-agents setup' and restarting your agent; it should only be used on open-source software or devices/apps you own, since reverse engineering often violates terms of service

Workflow 1 - Game Modding: the 'universal-modder' plugin for Claude Code (requires Python 3.10+, ffmpeg, Git) auto-locates a game's engine, builds mods, generates sprites/audio, and tests them live (e.g., adding a homing missile launcher to Terraria)

Workflow 2 - Competitor Teardowns: REA can reveal how a competitor's feature works internally (e.g., whether a search feature queries on every keystroke or uses a local cached index), then build only the minimal components needed for your own project after confirming permission

Workflow 3 - Device Control Apps: REA can examine how a device's proprietary app communicates with hardware (e.g., an AC unit) and wrap those controls in an MCP to build a custom interface, after first checking for an official API

items.title: Apple bans AI 'nudify' apps from the App Store
points: New Rule 1.2 explicitly bans AI apps that generate or distribute nonconsensual intimate imagery, requiring developers to actively prevent and remove such content or face removal
New guideline 2.5.19 targets developers who hide nudify features during review then activate them post-approval, risking permanent ban from the App Store and Developer Program
Earlier this year Apple threatened to remove xAI's Grok over nude deepfakes; Grok was later re-approved after adding safeguards

items.title: Anthropic AI solves a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery
points: Anthropic's internal model identified five mysterious seeds the NSA distributed in the late 1990s, matching them to lrand48 (an older C library random-number generator) using 1997-1998 timestamps in under 30 minutes
The AI found the P-256 curve's published seed at the 1,842nd candidate position, making a hidden NSA backdoor in NIST curves significantly less likely
Researchers still can't explain why the generator skipped some candidates; bitcoin's secp256k1 curve was never implicated

items.title: Anthropic proposes federal AI safety bill
points: The bill would require independent evaluators to flag risks to the Commerce Department within 72 hours before model deployment

items.title: Windows 11 performance boost
points: Microsoft promises up to 20% faster system responsiveness and improved memory efficiency, especially benefiting 8GB machines

items.title: Fake WhatsApp app evades Google Play detection
points: The fake app got over 500,000 downloads by exploiting Google Play's Early Access program, which hides user reviews during that phase

items.title: CoreWeave debt crisis rattles AI stock market
points: CoreWeave, a cloud infrastructure provider renting GPU compute (graphics processing units used for AI workloads) to clients, has accumulated $51 billion in debt, with default insurance costs jumping 33% in one week
CEO Mike Intrator cited a backlog exceeding $100 billion from clients including Microsoft, Meta, and IBM, but analysts warn actual cash flows must still materialize
The debt concerns spooked investors across AI stocks and chipmakers in a single trading day despite CoreWeave's strong customer pipeline

issues.subject: 🔥 You can finally reverse engineer any app

headlines: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) is a new GitHub tool that lets AI agents decompile and rebuild features from any app, enabling game modding, competitor teardowns, and custom device control software

sections.title: What REA Does and How to Set It Up
points: REA is an MCP server (a protocol that lets AI agents access external tools) that decompiles apps by converting compiled code back into human-readable pseudocode
It works iteratively: you ask your agent to analyze a feature, REA returns pseudocode with evidence, and your agent refines until the feature is fully rebuilt without copying original code
Setup requires running 'npx rea-agents setup' and restarting your agent—only use it on open-source software or devices/apps you own, as reverse engineering often violates terms of service

sections.title: Workflow 1: Game Modding with Claude Code
points: Install the 'universal-modder' plugin for Claude Code with dependencies Python 3.10+, ffmpeg, and Git
The plugin automatically locates the game engine, inspects code, builds mods, generates sprites and audio, and tests everything live in-game
Example: add a homing missile launcher and tactical nuke to Terraria by describing the mod; the agent handles the implementation end-to-end

sections.title: Workflow 2: Reverse Engineer Competitor Features
points: Use REA to understand how a competitor's app (like a notes app's instant search) actually works—revealing whether it queries on every keystroke or uses a local index (cached data you can access without network calls)
Send your agent a prompt that verifies you have permission to analyze the app, traces findings to specific code files, and outlines a plan before writing
Once approved, your agent builds only the minimum components you need for your own project, avoiding code duplication

sections.title: Workflow 3: Build Better Device Control Apps
points: REA can examine how a device's proprietary app communicates with hardware (like an AC unit), then wrap those controls in an MCP (protocol)
Build a custom interface (e.g., Mac menu-bar app) that drives the device without relying on the vendor's app
The prompt first checks for an official API to avoid reverse engineering when a supported option exists
